You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure described in the bug report is that the MultiDirectional optimization loops forever if the starting point is already the correct solution. The failing test `testMinimizeMaximize` shows a minimization where the optimizer is started near a known solution and seems to not terminate as expected.

Looking at the code for `MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex(Comparator<RealPointValuePair>)`, the optimization logic is inside an infinite `while (true)` loop. Within each iteration, it tries to improve the simplex by reflection, expansion, or contraction steps. If any of these yield an improvement (compared with the current best vertex), the simplex is updated and the method returns (terminates the iteration).

However, if no improvement is found (i.e., the reflected point is not better than the best, and the contracted point is also not better than the best), the loop simply repeats. There is no breaking condition when the simplex cannot be improved any further (i.e., if the current point is already optimal). In that scenario, the `while (true)` loop never exits, causing an infinite loop.

This matches the bug report that the loop runs forever if the starting point is already the solution, since no improvement steps shrink or otherwise move the simplex. Also, the test code has a tight convergence checker but the iterateSimplex method itself does not include any convergence check or termination criteria when the simplex points do not improve.

Furthermore, the `evaluateNewSimplex` method creates new transformed simplices by moving the vertices relative to the best vertex and evaluates the new points but there is no logic in `iterateSimplex` to handle the case when no new simplex is better than the current one besides continuing the infinite loop.

In summary, the issue is that the termination condition inside `iterateSimplex` depends solely on improvement steps, and when none occur (already optimal start), the infinite loop does not break leading to the freeze or hang described in the current bug report.

Recent bug reports are unrelated.

Recommendation is to add an explicit convergence or no-improvement termination condition in `iterateSimplex` to break the loop and avoid infinite execution when optimization stalls because starting at solution or optimizer stuck.

This explains the observed test failure, the infinite optimize loop, and matches the report description.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
